players.product: dedicated bare-metal AI infrastructure (GPU clusters) designed, deployed, owned and operated for enterprises; Axe Compute Build build-to-order program

quarterly_data.signal: Axe Compute's 10-K (fiscal 2025) describes its compute business as asset-light - it did not own or operate physical data centers - with revenue from Compute Services generated primarily through reserved GPU capacity contracts under which customers commit to capacity on a prepaid basis, typically under 12- to 36-month terms, priced per GPU per hour, plus ancillary storage and CPU services; it works with hardware and infrastructure providers across a network of over 200 locations. Fiscal 2025 revenue of $125,284 came entirely from the Drug Discovery Services segment (the Compute Services and Treasury Management segment had no revenue); net loss was $233,095,203, including $152,490,550 of losses on digital assets and a $52,735,000 loss on derivative instruments.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 revenue $125,284; net loss $233,095,203; losses on digital assets $152,490,550; over 200 locations; 12- to 36-month prepaid terms

players.product: GB200 / GB300 / Vera Rubin GPU systems

connects_to.relationship: B300 / GB300 NVL72 GPUs and NVIDIA switching for Axe Compute GPU clusters

contracts.signal: Axe Compute's 10-K: it sources GPU hardware primarily from NVIDIA Corporation and does not manufacture any hardware itself; the loss of or significant disruption to its access to NVIDIA GPU supply could materially delay its ability to fulfill customer orders.
